# core/format.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/format.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Building text out of pieces: padding into columns,
joining, replacing, quoting, and sizes a person can read. Every function
appends to a text (`Vec[u8]`, see core/text.bastio); numbers come from
core/num.bastio.

What is proved: each function keeps the bytes already in the text, and the
ones that repeat, pad or copy say exactly how many bytes they add and what
they are. Not proved: the exact bytes of `fmt_join`, `fmt_replace_all`,
`fmt_quoted` and `fmt_size` (tests check them).

`import "core/format.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`fmt_repeat`](#fmt_repeat) | Appends `n` copies of the byte `c`. |
| [`fmt_pad_left`](#fmt_pad_left) | Appends `b`, preceded by spaces so that at least `width` bytes are added. |
| [`fmt_pad_right`](#fmt_pad_right) | Appends `b`, followed by spaces so that at least `width` bytes are added. |
| [`fmt_bool`](#fmt_bool) | Appends `true` or `false`. |
| [`fmt_join`](#fmt_join) | Appends the pieces `parts` of `src` (what `bytes_split` and `lines_split` return) with `sep` between them. |
| [`fmt_replace_all`](#fmt_replace_all) | Appends `hay` with every occurrence of `needle` replaced by `with`. |
| [`fmt_quoted`](#fmt_quoted) | Appends `b` in double quotes, with `"` and `\` escaped by a backslash, newline, return and tab as `\n`, `\r` and `\t`, and any other byte outside the printable ASCII range as `\xHH`. |
| [`fmt_size`](#fmt_size) | Appends a byte count a person can read. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `fmt_repeat`

```bastio
fn fmt_repeat(t: &mut Vec[u8], c: u8, n: u64)
  ensures vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + n
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
  ensures forall k: u64 :: k < n ==> vget(t, vlen(old(t)) + k) == c
```

Appends `n` copies of the byte `c`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_repeat(&mut t, 45, 5);   // '-'
assert vlen(t) == 5 && vget(t, 4) == 45;
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "-----");
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_pad_left`

```bastio
fn fmt_pad_left(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes, width: u64)
  ensures blen(b) >= width ==> vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + blen(b)
  ensures blen(b) < width ==> vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + width
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `b`, preceded by spaces so that at least `width` bytes are added:
a right-aligned column.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("ab");
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_pad_left(&mut t, name, 5);
fmt_pad_left(&mut t, name, 1);   // already wider than 1: no padding
assert vlen(t) == 7;
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "   abab");
bfree(b);
bfree(name);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_pad_right`

```bastio
fn fmt_pad_right(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes, width: u64)
  ensures blen(b) >= width ==> vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + blen(b)
  ensures blen(b) < width ==> vlen(t) == vlen(old(t)) + width
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `b`, followed by spaces so that at least `width` bytes are added:
a left-aligned column.

Example:

```bastio
let name = bfrom("ab");
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_pad_right(&mut t, name, 4);
text_push(&mut t, 124);   // '|'
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "ab  |");
bfree(b);
bfree(name);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_bool`

```bastio
fn fmt_bool(t: &mut Vec[u8], v: bool)
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `true` or `false`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_bool(&mut t, true);
text_push(&mut t, 47);   // '/'
fmt_bool(&mut t, false);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "true/false");
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_join`

```bastio
fn fmt_join(t: &mut Vec[u8], src: &Bytes, parts: &Vec[Span], sep: &Bytes)
  requires forall k: u64 :: k < vlen(parts) ==> span_in(vget(parts, k), src)
  ensures vlen(t) >= vlen(old(t))
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends the pieces `parts` of `src` (what `bytes_split` and
`lines_split` return) with `sep` between them.

Example:

```bastio
let src = bfrom("usr:local:bin");
let parts = bytes_split(src, 58);   // ':'
let sep = bfrom("/");
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_join(&mut t, src, parts, sep);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "usr/local/bin");
bfree(b);
bfree(sep);
vec_free(parts);
bfree(src);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_replace_all`

```bastio
fn fmt_replace_all(t: &mut Vec[u8], hay: &Bytes, needle: &Bytes, with: &Bytes)
  requires blen(needle) > 0
  ensures vlen(t) >= vlen(old(t))
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `hay` with every occurrence of `needle` replaced by `with`.
Occurrences do not overlap and are found from the left, so replacing `aa`
in `aaa` leaves one `a` after the replacement.

Example:

```bastio
let hay = bfrom("a-b-c");
let needle = bfrom("-");
let with = bfrom(" -- ");
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_replace_all(&mut t, hay, needle, with);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "a -- b -- c");
bfree(b);
bfree(with);
bfree(needle);
bfree(hay);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_quoted`

```bastio
fn fmt_quoted(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes)
  ensures vlen(t) >= vlen(old(t)) + 2
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends `b` in double quotes, with `"` and `\` escaped by a backslash,
newline, return and tab as `\n`, `\r` and `\t`, and any other byte outside
the printable ASCII range as `\xHH`.

Example:

```bastio
let raw = bfrom("say \"hi\"\n");
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_quoted(&mut t, raw);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "\"say \\\"hi\\\"\\n\"");
bfree(b);
bfree(raw);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `fmt_size`

```bastio
fn fmt_size(t: &mut Vec[u8], n: u64)
  ensures vlen(t) > vlen(old(t))
  ensures text_keeps(t, old(t), vlen(old(t)))
```

Appends a byte count a person can read: `512 B`, `1.5 KiB`, `3.0 MiB`,
up to `EiB`. One digit follows the point, rounded down.

Example:

```bastio
let mut t = text_new();
fmt_size(&mut t, 512);
text_push(&mut t, 44);
fmt_size(&mut t, 1536);
text_push(&mut t, 44);
fmt_size(&mut t, 3 * 1048576);
let b = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "512 B,1.5 KiB,3.0 MiB");
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```
